description.narrative: Taxing Efficient for Developing Inclusive (TEDI) is the revenue reform component of the FCDO-funded program for tax and financial management 2018-2024 and supports more inclusive economic growth through government revenues, public investment, debt management and financial planning in the medium to long term. Mozambique Revenue Authority (MRA, tax administration) and the Ministry of Finance (MEF, responsible for tax policy) receive support through technical assistance and related procurement of goods and service under a service contract with the canadian company CoWater. Under the tax administration component, TEDI supports the areas of tax auditing, taxation of extractive resources and broadening of the tax base. In tax policy, TEDI supports MEF to begin exercising its mandate for tax policy analysis and formulation.

Mocambique Revenue Authority (MRA, skatteförvaltning) och finansministeriet (MEF, ansvarig för skattepolitik) får stöd genom teknisk assistans och relaterad upphandling av varor och tjänster under ett serviceavtal med det kanadensiska företaget CoWater. Under skatteförvaltningsdelen stödjer TEDI områdena skatterevision, beskattning av utvinningsresurser och breddning av skattebasen. The Taxing Efficiently for Developing Inclusively (TEDI) programme is the revenue reform component of the FCDO-funded Tax and Economic Governance (TEG) Programme. TEDI is a £12 million programme, currently scheduled to operate from January 2020 to June 2025, supporting the Mozambican Revenue Authority (MRA) and the Ministry of Economy of Finance (MEF) through the provision of technical assistance and procurement of goods and services (a £3 million Procurement Fund). The programme is based on a resident full-time team, supported by part-time and short-term international and national experts. As of December 2022, the TEDI programme is jointly funded by FCDO and Sida.
The overall programmes intended impact is to support the Government of Mozambique (GoM) in its ability to self-finance its economic and social development through increased, sustainable revenue collection.
The programme works across the following outputs:
1) Tax Administration, providing technical assistance specifically on tax audit to the MRAs Audit Department (DiAFT);
2) Extractives, providing technical assistance to the MRAs Extractives Industry Taxation Unit (EITU);
3) Tax Policy, providing technical assistance to the MEF, specifically the National Directorate of Economic Policies and Development (DNPED); and
4) Gender, Equality, and Social Inclusion (GESI), providing support to the MRAs Communications and Image Unit (GCIm) on taxpayer communications and education as well as mainstreaming GESI considerations, particularly within tax policy.

description.narrative:
Main achievements
* A major milestone was the formal approval of the national revenue strategy in early July 2025, which incorporated several TEDI recommendations based on its earlier diagnostic of the Mozambique tax system.
* through TEDIs advocacy, the program has also contributed to the formal establishment of a new directorate for fiscal and financial studies in Ministry of Finance. Tax Policy will be part of the responsibility of this new directorate.
* TEDI also delivered analysis on Value Added Tax (VAT) exemptions, and provided support for analysis of the development plans and economic models for the two FLNG (Floating Liquefied Natural Gas) projects Coral Sul and Coral Norte.
* the pricing platform Bloomberg was, after several delays, successfully contracted, with the active use of the database producing the June and July Mineral Reference Price Bulletins (MRPB). Increased Extractives Revenue is expected as a result of this, by applying internationally bench marked reference prices (IRP) to mineral exports.
* the MRA Board has approved GESI communication products (leaflets on ISPC, simplified VAT, second category IRPS, and a taxpayer guide), jointly developed with TEDI. The MRAs Communications and Image Unit (GCIm) has also validated the methodology for designing a Do No Harm strategy for taxpayer education.
* TEDI has moved forward with the Compliance Risk Management (CRM) training, which not only facilitated the long-awaited validation of the sector notes by the MRA, but also enabled participants to identify sector-specific risks. The training was delivered regionally, with an emphasis on industries most relevant to each location, enhancing the practical relevance of the sessions.
* there has been progress in operationalising the IRRM, a tax introduced in 2014 to capture super-profits in Mozambiques mining sector.
* as a result of targeted capacity-building efforts, EITU staff (Extractives Industry Taxation Unit) are now better equipped to conduct Transfer Pricing (TP) analysis and oversight within the extractive sector, a crucial step in mitigating revenue losses from profit shifting and tax base erosion.
* monitoring visits to extractive companies in Maputo and Zambézia provinces operating in commodities such as bentonite, tantalite, manganese, beryl, lepidolite, pollucite, and heavy sands revealed significant compliance issues with tax regulations and operational challenge. These findings provided immediate enforcement opportunities, which are likely to generate additional tax revenues for Mozambique.
* the submission of the complete draft of the Tax Policy Diagnostic was a result of two years work to comprehensively analyse the principal taxes and propose recommendations for reform. These recommendations were distilled into a practical roadmap for reform, annexed to the diagnostic, which could serve as a basis for reforms to be implemented by the new government.
* the policy note on fiscal benefits to stimulate discussion led to a request for a comprehensive analysis of the current context, followed by a proposed legal drafting reflecting TEDIs recommendations to the Fiscal Benefits Code.
* the delivery of a Tax Data Flow mapping, which aims to increase the ability to carry out evidence-based tax policy by improving access to data. The report highlights existing data flows and identifies the factors that make it impossible, difficult, or time-consuming to obtain certain data essential for tax policy analysis. As a result, MEF requested the project to draft an ofício - to be signed by the Minister of Finance - requiring data-holding institutions to share data with MEF on a regular basis.
* support to MEF on LNG contracts' fiscal conditions: TEDI has initiated support to an embedded advisor working on this topic, focusing on the implementation of the Sovereign Wealth Fund (SWF), as well as monitoring/forecasting LNG revenues. Two deliverables have already been completed - an analysis of the Coral Sul contracts identifying conditions that could be altered for future contracts, and a review of the data required by MEF to monitor LNG revenues.
* TEDI was given the opportunity to contribute to the drafting of the five-year Public Financial Management Strategy (PFM), to ensure tax policy is adequately reflected. .
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
